why: The repo is an operating system, not a media locker. Git holds knowledge; media lives outside. This file is the single source of truth for that rule, and scripts/media-check.mjs + .github/workflows/repo-guard.yml enforce it.

principle.git_holds: text — knowledge, skills, docs, config, code, measurements, and one small line per media file
principle.git_does_not_hold: media binaries — video, audio, image plates, 3D models, archives
principle.every_media_gets: an index line (path, bytes, sha256, where-it-lives, why-it-matters) so nothing is lost when the binary leaves Git

size_gate.hard_fail_note: GitHub rejects any single file over 100 MB. 100,000,000 is GitHub's own threshold, not 104857600.
size_gate.warn_note: 20 MB is the point where someone should ask 'is this knowledge or media?'

repo_budget.warn_human: 1.5 GB — approaching the point where clones get slow

outside_git_roots.why: regenerable scratch: frames, decoded audio, browser bundles
transient clones used for skill vendoring

keep_in_git.note: These are small, they are the product surface, and they break the site if removed. They are exempt from the media rule.

upload_limits.connector_note: The Drive/Dropbox upload tools in this environment refuse files over 100 MB. This is a hard ceiling on any automatable upload path.
upload_limits.consequence: A 12-minute video must be encoded at or below ~1.1 Mbps VBR to stay under 100 MB. Measured reference: the existing 12-minute 3D 1080p film in deliverables/ is 63 MB.
upload_limits.verified_note: Only ~50 MB has actually been exercised end to end. Anything larger is untested; test before promising it.

longform_1080p.arithmetic: (0.85 + 0.128) Mbps x 720 s / 8 x 1.08 overhead = 95.1 MB, inside the 100 MB ceiling with 4.9 MB to spare
longform_1080p.note: 0.85 Mbps is generous next to the 0.7 Mbps master already shipped. Rendered 3D animation has large flat regions and slow camera moves, so it compresses far better than live action at the same perceptual quality. YouTube re-encodes every upload, so a fatter master buys no visible quality — it only costs upload time, phone storage and sandbox disk.

delivery_flow: render inside the sandbox, targeting the encode_targets above
upload to Drive into the channel folder recorded in config/drive-map.json
add one line to deliverables/INDEX.md: file, bytes, sha256, Drive link, what it is, what it teaches
hand the link to the operator for the YouTube upload (Studio can import from Drive directly)
delete the sandbox copy only after the index line exists and the Drive upload is confirmed
never: force-push without a git bundle backup of --all
delete a file to free space without an index line proving where the surviving copy is
promise an upload size that has not been tested at that size

regenerable_evidence.principle: Some tracked images are not creative assets — they are measurement output extracted from an already-released master. They are reproducible from the master with a script that is already in the repo, so keeping them in Git stores the answer twice and the question once.
regenerable_evidence.requirement: A folder may be treated as regenerable evidence only if it contains BOTH (a) the script that produces it and (b) a manifest pinning the exact source (sha256 of the master). Otherwise it is creative work and stays.
regenerable_evidence.regenerate_command: python <folder>/extract_evidence.py   # run from repo root after restoring the pinned master into .cache/

folders.why_csv_stays: the CSVs are the measurements themselves in text form — kilobytes, diffable, citable. The JPGs are a rendering of the same numbers.
folders.source_sha256_from: hardcoded assert at the top of review-v13/extract_evidence.py
production/extinct-life/review-v14/EVIDENCE.json asset_sha256 (226 MB master), re-verified by the script against film-v14-directed/QC.json
folders.why_csv_stays: the CSVs are the measurements themselves in text form — kilobytes, diffable, citable. The JPGs are a rendering of the same numbers.

regenerable_evidence.not_regenerable: film-v*-dir/*/inspection/ and */inspection/ stills are copied from .cache/ by the producing workflow (cp -r .cache/extinct-v14/stills production/...). They are outputs of a render, not of a script with a pinned source, so they are not covered here and stay until their owning workflow is changed to upload instead of commit.

workflow_handoff.problem: 20 of the 42 workflows that commit use `git add production/extinct-life/<film>`, `git add docs/research/assets/...` or `git add deliverables/<name>.mp4` — they push inspection stills and evidence frames straight into Git on every run. That is the mechanism that keeps regrowing the repo. Adding an ignore rule while they still do this would fail their commits; changing them all at once is a 20-workflow change that needs each one verified.
workflow_handoff.rule: A workflow that produces media must upload it (GitHub Actions artifact or Drive), not commit it. `scripts/check-workflow-media.mjs` reports which ones still commit.
workflow_handoff.worst_offender: extinct-feature-3d.yml does `git add deliverables/Extinct_Life_3D_Chapter03_Production_1080p.mp4` — a video file added to Git by name, deliberately, in a workflow

migration_precedent.result: git rm --cached ran; file remains on disk at the same path; Drive copy verified byte-for-byte by sha256
migration_precedent.why_this_matters: proves the whole loop end to end before touching 25 more files: upload -> verify hash -> release from Git -> file still present on disk
